questions.prompt: A frozen encoder is used with a linear probe. What does the probe's held-out accuracy measure?
questions.skillLabel: Evaluating an embedding with a probe
options: The number of parameters in the encoder.
How well the training loss of the encoder decreased.
How readable the downstream task is from the embedding.
Whether the images are the same size.
questions.explanation: A probe isolates the representation: a simple model reads the task from frozen features.

questions.prompt: Compute cos(a,b) for a=(3,4), b=(4,3). Give 3 decimals.
InfoNCE with tau=0.5, one positive (cos 0.8) and two negatives (cos 0 and -1). Give the loss to 3 decimals.
A contrastive encoder collapses so every image maps to the same vector. With 1 positive and 7 negatives, the InfoNCE loss is
questions.explanation: All logits are equal, so the positive has probability 1/8 and the loss is ln 8.

questions.prompt: You have 300 labelled images from a domain very different from ImageNet. Which is the most defensible first experiment?
options: Train a new network from scratch on the 300 images with heavy augmentation.
Fine-tune all layers with a large learning rate on the 300 labelled images.
Skip evaluation of transfer, since pretraining always transfers to any domain.
Linear probe on frozen features, compared with an untrained-encoder baseline.
questions.explanation: Small data and a different domain: avoid destroying pretrained features, use probes and baselines.

questions.prompt: A frozen probe scores 0.94 on a random split of the source domain and 0.61 on a different camera. Give the in-domain minus shifted gap (2 decimals).
Design a held-out-domain evaluation for an encoder that will be used on a gripper camera. State the sets, baseline, metric and a rejection rule.
rubric: Names an in-domain set and a genuinely different held-out set.
Includes a baseline (majority-class or untrained encoder) and the metric.
States a rejection rule or boundary case for the shifted accuracy.
questions.explanation: Rubric-guided: compare your answer with each rubric point; this question is not automatically graded.
